London System

How to read the board

Every line uses the same visual language, so the colours teach you patterns — not noise.

Colours

Green — the main line, recommended piece paths, good squares
Blue — accepted alternatives and playable variant moves
Red — the opponent’s threats, blunders, forbidden squares, lines to avoid
Yellow — interesting but secondary plans, inaccuracies
Orange — poor moves, weak or dangerous squares, poor pieces

Arrow style

Solid — a direct, immediate attack or defence (or the move just played)
Dashed — a potential manoeuvre that depends on the next move
Thick — a move that wins material (dashed + thick = a future material win)

Circles & squares

Green circle — strong square / target for us
Blue circle — alternative square
Red circle — mined or forbidden square, piece under fire
Orange circle — weak square or poorly placed piece
Last-move squares: green ✓ book move
blue !? playable, but not the book move
yellow ?! inaccuracy
orange ? mistake
red ?? blunder

How training works

  1. 📖 Study (basic lines): step through with Next/Back — every move is explained.
  2. 🎯 Guided (all other lines): you play every move yourself, with the explanation of the last move, 💡 hints and ◀ to look back.
  3. ⚔ No help: from memory. A wrong move is punished by the opponent; step ◀ ▶ through the punishment and the engine line, then retry. Switch modes with the badge under the line title.
  4. Every mistake is recorded: ✗ Mistake drill replays exactly those positions. Lines played cleanly without help enter 🔁 Spaced review (1, 3, 7, 14… days).
  5. ♾ Survival: random lines without help until your first mistake. 📜 Master games: replay annotated games or guess the winner’s moves. The Learn tab has lessons and puzzles.
Evaluations: Stockfish 19, depth 13–18. Pieces: Colin M.L. Burnett (cburnett), CC BY-SA 3.0.
